answer: Here is one mechanism that works: attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because onyx only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, kernel is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any mirror approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
